title: Calibrating a syringe pump by gravimetry
content:
A syringe pump computes plunger speed from the syringe inner diameter you program. Real syringes — 3D-printed or commercial — have diameter tolerance, so the delivered flow can be off by several percent even though the pump is mechanically accurate. In our tests a "3 mL" syringe with a nominal 8.94 mm bore actually delivered +2.5 %; the corrected diameter was 9.05 mm. This gravimetric calibration needs only an analytical balance — no flow sensor. Water weighs ~1 g/mL, so 1 mg ≈ 1 µL: the balance gives real dispensed volume directly. 
Q_real = mass / (ρ_water · time)
D_real = D₀ · √(Q_real / Q_set)
If the balance reads more flow than programmed → the syringe is wider than you told the pump → increase the diameter. Enter D_real and the pump delivers true flow. The calculator calibrate.py does the math — you just type the numbers you measured. Equipment Analytical balance, 1 mg (0.001 g); 0.1 mg is even better. Syringe under test, filled with bubble-free distilled water. Parafilm + a small receiving tube (e.g. Eppendorf). Tweezers/tongs for handling calibration weights (skin oil weighs enough to matter). The syringe pump (this project). Step 0 — Calibrate the balance (once) Place it on a stable, level table (centre the bubble with the feet); no drafts, sun or vibration. Warm it up for ≥ 1 hour powered on. Empty pan, reading 0.0. Enter external calibration (on CGOLDENWALL/JoanLab HZ-type balances: Set → menu → e-cal; it requests a standard weight, e.g. cal-200 = 200 g). Place the exact standard weight with tongs, wait, remove when prompted → returns to 0.0. Verify: place a known weight (e.g. 100 g) and check it reads correctly. Step 1 — Prepare the run Fill the syringe, purge all air (a single bubble ruins a run). Mount it in the pump. Program the nominal diameter D₀ (caliper the inner bore, or use the syringe spec) and the target flow Q_set. Let the pump drip into any waste tube until the flow is steady — we use 5 min; the first minutes clear residual bubbles and let the mechanics settle. Step 2 — Collect the output, weighed (timed collection) Prepare the collection tube first: close the empty Eppendorf, seal the top with parafilm, pierce a small hole with the sharp tip of scissors (just big enough for the capillary — keeps evaporation low), and stand it on a small, very light base (we cut one from the foam used to pack boxes — negligible mass, keeps the round-bottom tube upright on the pan). Weigh it in this final state (tube + parafilm + hole + foam base) → m_empty, or tare to zero. Then collect, without stopping the flow: with the flow already steady (Step 1), move the capillary from the waste tube into the collection tube through the parafilm hole, and start the stopwatch at that instant. Collect for an exactly timed interval t (t goes straight into the result). Move the capillary out, press the parafilm closed over the hole, and weigh immediately → m_full. Δm = m_full − m_empty.

1 — Caliper the bore to get the nominal diameter D₀
2 — Seal the tube top with parafilm
3 — Pierce a small hole with a scissor tip
4 — Insert the capillary through the hole
Aim for Δm ≥ 100 mg (e.g. 10 min at 1000 µL/h ≈ 167 mg → <1 % uncertainty at 1 mg). Step 3 — Compute and correct ➡️ Open the web calculator — type the weighed values, get the corrected diameter (no install). 
python3 calibrate.py --d0 8.94 --qset 1000 --mass 170.5 --minutes 10 --temp 20
#   flow real (balance): 1024.8 uL/h  (+2.5 %)
#   CORRECTED DIAMETER : 9.05 mm   <- enter this on the pump
Enter D_real on the pump. Repeat one point to confirm Q_real ≈ Q_set. Step 4 — Verify linearity Repeat at 2–3 flows (e.g. 500 / 1000 / 2000 µL/h) with the corrected diameter. If they all give the same D_real, the calibration is solid and flow-independent. Practical tips (what ruins a run) Evaporation: at 1000 µL/h an open tube loses ~1 mg/min — always parafilm, and weigh immediately after capping. Weights with tongs, never fingers. Exclude the first ~5 min of each run (stabilization + bubble clearing). Record water temperature; the tool adjusts density (20 °C → 0.99821 g/mL). ±2 °C is negligible (<0.1 %). Bubbles: purge before, and if the output suddenly spikes/dips erratically, there is air in the line — stop and purge. Optional: cross-check with a flow sensor (higher precision) The balance fixes the diameter. If you also have an in-line flow sensor, the same runs let you check — and calibrate — the sensor against the balance (ground truth), and then use the sensor as a continuous flow reference without weighing every time. calibrate.py reports the sensor factor if you pass --sensor-ulh <reading>. For the flow-sensor hardware, firmware and high-rate acquisition, see the Rio controller: ➡️ wenzel-lab/rio-controller (pressure/flow module). Tool: calibrate.py · rev 2026-11-19
